messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — we're seeing a bunch of worker traces start as new roots after gateway enqueues (SQS). Looks like traceparent isn't surviving our enqueue->dequeue path.

sam: Ugh. Are we using the W3C `traceparent` header or OTEL baggage?

maya: Gateway sets `traceparent` on HTTP inbound, captures span, then when we push to SQS we only put a short JSON payload, no headers. SQS message attributes currently only include `retries` and `payload-type`.

devon: I checked logs — when the worker pulls messages, it expects a `traceparent` header in the request metadata from the poller. But SQS doesn't have headers, so we lose it.

hector: Two options: 1) serialize span context into an SQS message attribute (string), 2) rely on a sidecar/poller that reattaches headers on dequeue. Both have tradeoffs (attr size limits, encoding).

liz: Attribute size is the kicker — SQS message attributes have a 256KB cap per message, but per-attribute keys have smaller practical limits. We should keep the context compact. W3C `traceparent` is small (55 chars-ish).

maya: Proposed minimal approach: gateway injects a `redwood-trace` attribute set to the W3C `traceparent` (plus a small `baggage`-encoded base64 if needed). Worker middleware prefers `traceparent` from HTTP if present, then falls back to message attribute `redwood-trace`.

sam: Sounds reasonable. Implementation note: use OpenTelemetry TextMapPropagator and a simple carrier that maps to message attributes. Example (JS pseudo):

```js
// carrier is simple object mapping
const carrier = { 'redwood-trace': msg.Attributes['redwood-trace'] };
const spanContext = propagator.extract(context.active(), carrier);
// start span with that ctx
```

devon: Also remember baggage. If we need small amounts, base64-encode `baggage` and attach `redwood-baggage`. But avoid large baggage or we should store in a fast KV and reference by key.

hector: Another gotcha: FIFO queues + dedup can rewrite message IDs — but attributes stay intact. Sidecar approach complicates scaling. I'd vote for attribute injection in gateway and worker extraction. Simpler and fewer moving parts.

liz: We should add a guard: if attribute > 8KB, drop and emit a metric/alert. Also add a config flag for "prefer-attributes" vs "prefer-header" for customers using private deployment with different queue tech.

maya: I'll prototype gateway middleware to set `redwood-trace` on enqueue ops and worker middleware to `extract` and `start` spans. I'll include unit tests for both OTEL JS and Go SDKs.

sam: For Go, quick sketch:

```go
carrier := sqscarrier{Attrs: msg.MessageAttributes}
ctx := propagators.TextMap.Propagator().Extract(context.Background(), carrier)
// use ctx to create span
```

devon: We also need to update our telemetry pipeline exporter mapping: if workers rehydrate spans, ensure exporter deduplicates or links children correctly. Add `span.kind` tags (producer/consumer) so tracing UI stitches them.

hector: Good point — set `span.kind=producer` on enqueue and `span.kind=consumer` on worker span. Also attach `message.id` and `queue.name` as attributes for easier debugging.

ops-bot: note: New alert rule "queue_trace_attr_overflow" will fire if `redwood-trace` attr exceeds 8KB 3 times in 5m in production queue.*

liz: Action items: Maya -> prototype + PR for gateway middleware; Devon -> worker middleware + tests; Sam -> docs/console setting for "queue tracing" toggle and retention note; Hector -> add span.kind conventions to tracing docs. I'll open tickets.

maya: Thanks — will ping when PR is up. If anyone has objections to the simple attribute approach, speak now, otherwise we'll run prototype in staging. :thumbsup:

sam: +1. Keep an eye on retention/ingestion — we might want to sample these queue-span pairs more aggressively to save costs.

maya: Noted. We'll add a config to map queue->sampling-rate in the middleware.

devon: Nice. Also consider adding a brief migration note in the console about how older messages won't have trace attrs and will show as new-root spans.

hector: One more: when we rehydrate, call `SetSpanAttributes` with `redwood.enqueue_time` (timestamp) so downstream trace shows latency in queue.

maya: Great suggestion. Ending thread — will file PR + tickets and tag owners.
